title: User & role control
evidence:
Layer 2 role model: built-in `role` is only admin/user (platform: live User read shows only h.josepablo@gmail.com holds `admin`). Tenant scoping and tenant role live in custom `User.tenant_id` and `User.app_role` (bar_admin | staff; super_admin is in the enum but unused). Deployed schema, read via list_entity_schemas on appId 6ab41c2a89f592a0eca074d2, matches base44/entities/User.jsonc: both fields have rls.write:false. Only createWineBar and manageStaff write them (base44/functions/createWineBar/entry.ts:40, manageStaff/entry.ts:144,199,212,283), all as service role. The two layers are not merged: the app has no reference to Mission Control's `members`.

Promote/demote (base44/functions/manageStaff/entry.ts, setRole around line 170-200): the caller must be bar_admin, or platform admin, per a fresh service-role read of the stored profile (line 43, module 22). Promote and demote share one path and one gate, `checkSetRole` in _member_logic.ts. It returns owner_locked, last_admin (a demote that would leave zero bar_admin returns 409), and not_found for a target outside the caller's tenant. Unit tests are in base44/tests/staff_members_logic_test.ts. `invite` only honors bar_admin if the caller is bar_admin (entry.ts:105).

Joining: emailed invite is admin-initiated (`invite` action, StaffInvite row plus own email, 14-day expiry, one row per tenant+email, revokeInvite). `claimInvite` looks up by the caller's STORED email, revokes the person's other pending invites, and refuses if already in a bar. Direct assignment to an existing unassigned User is refused with 409 if the user is in another bar. There is no open self-join. The standard only requires one of code or emailed invite.

Module 24 check: `node scripts/check-tenant-roles.mjs` prints "Module 24 — no tenant role reaches every tenant"; `validate:tenant-roles` is wired in .github/workflows. Live users: 1 platform admin, 2 tenants, roles consistent. StaffInvite RLS is admin-only for writes and tenant-scoped for reads.

gaps.what: No single file declares the role mapping. The standard says the app's role model is 'kept in one file' (puntos' src/lib/rbac.js). Sommel has 'bar_admin' and 'staff' literals spread over src/components/Layout.jsx, src/components/staff/MemberActions.jsx, src/pages/Staff.jsx, src/lib/permissionRegistry.js, and six copies of the server _guard.ts plus manageStaff/_member_logic.ts and _invite_logic.ts. permissionRegistry.js is the de facto declaration for permissions, but not for role names and their labels. This is cosmetic, not a security hole.
gaps.fix: Add src/lib/rbac.js exporting ROLES ({bar_admin, staff}), the platform check, the labels ('Admin' / 'Mesero'), isBarAdmin(user) and isPlatform(user). Replace the client literals with it. Optionally have the check:guards generator verify the server copy.

gaps.what: The `super_admin` value in the User.app_role enum is dead: nothing in src/ or base44/ (excluding tests) writes or reads it. It is a leftover role name that muddies the 'small, named set of roles' and the platform tier, which is already expressed by built-in role 'admin'.
gaps.fix: Remove 'super_admin' from the enum in User.jsonc, after confirming that no live row uses it (the live read showed none), and deploy the entity schema with the repo's deploy:entities script.
gaps.blocked_on: deploy:entities needs a Base44-authenticated CLI

gaps.what: The last-admin guard is a read-then-write with no conditional update. A concurrent demote or remove of two admins could each see 2 admins and both pass, leaving zero. The code itself acknowledges this kind of race for invite (entry.ts, 'a sub-second race remains'). It is low probability because it needs two admins acting at the same moment.
gaps.fix: After a demote or remove, re-read the tenant's admin count. If it is 0, restore the actor's target to bar_admin and return 409 last_admin. This is best-effort, since Base44 has no transactions.

title: License lifecycle (owned centrally by Mission Control)
evidence:
Done: no native lifecycle cron/function exists in sommel (base44/functions has only attendance, catalog, createWineBar, inventory, manageStaff, orders, payments, printing, processSale, reports, settings, shifts, stations). WineBar.billing_status enum is exactly trial|active|view_only|suspended. The deployed schema was read live with list_entity_schemas (app 6ab41c2a89f592a0eca074d2) and matches base44/entities/WineBar.jsonc. billing_status, trial_end_at, current_period_end, plan and owner_id all carry rls.write role:admin, which is the module's verification gate. base44/functions/createWineBar/entry.ts sets billing_status 'trial' and trial_end_at = server Date.now() + 30 days as a service role. The user already having a tenant returns 409. Server writes are gated: requireWritable in each function's _guard.ts returns 402 read_only for view_only/suspended (also manageStaff/entry.ts lines 88 and 171). The client maps read_only to friendly messages (PunchEntry.jsx, memberErrors.js).
Gaps: (1) grep of /home/user/acacia-mission-control finds no 'sommel' in supabase/migrations, api/_lib or src, so I found no apps registry row or adapter config for sommel. I did not query the live MC Supabase, so a row could exist there. (2) createWineBar sends no new_tenant ping to MC. There is no acaciaControl function, no tenant-pull, and no signing helper in sommel. (3) SuperAdmin.jsx line 36 writes WineBar.billing_status directly from the browser (own TODO comment), a second in-app write path beside MC. (4) The UI does not degrade for view_only/suspended: the only client reference to billing_status is SuperAdmin.jsx, with no banner and no disabled controls. Users only see errors after a write fails. (5) The 30-day trial constant is duplicated inline in createWineBar, which is acceptable but has no test. Not verified: MC live registry and bodega, and any authenticated session.

gaps.what: No evidence Sommel is registered in Mission Control (no apps row or adapter mapping for entity WineBar, so the lifecycle cron cannot reach billing_status). No acaciaControl bridge function exists in the sommel repo to read or write the tenant.
gaps.fix: Add base44/functions/acaciaControl (ping, license get/set patch on WineBar, tenants list, using the shared _acaciaSign.ts from acacia-app-standard/shared/bridge and ACACIA_APP_SLUG=sommel). Then run onboard:base44 in MC and insert the apps row. Confirm the row and a licence sync against the live MC Supabase.
gaps.blocked_on: Mission Control repo write access (registry row and adapter config), plus the INGEST_HMAC_SECRET and ACACIA_APP_SLUG secrets set in Base44 and Vercel. The bridge function itself overlaps modules 5, 15 and 17.

gaps.what: createWineBar creates a tenant without the new_tenant ping to MC (module 1's self-serve half). MC's daily sync is the only net.
gaps.fix: After WineBar.create, fire-and-forget a POST to MC /api/ingest/tenant-pull with {app:'sommel', tenantId: bar.id}, signed with the per-app key and ending in .catch(() => {}), so it never blocks onboarding. Copy StockFlow's signup call site.
gaps.blocked_on: Depends on the bridge signing helper and secrets from the gap above.

gaps.what: SuperAdmin.jsx writes billing_status straight from the browser via WineBar.update. This is a second in-app path that changes commercial state outside MC or a Safe function. The code says it is a known exception (a platform-only admin gate) and admits it violates the contract.
gaps.fix: Remove the status Select, or make it read-only, and let the platform owner change status in MC's admin UI through the bridge. If it stays, route it through a service-role function that checks the platform owner and audits the change.
gaps.blocked_on: User decision: keep the in-app override as a manual admin action, which the standard allows, or drop it. Not blocking if it is kept.

gaps.what: The UI does not degrade for view_only or suspended. There is no banner, and controls are not disabled. Users only find out through a 402 read_only error after trying to write. The standard says these states 'degrade the UI, not 500 it'.
gaps.fix: Expose the bar's billing_status to the client (WineBar read for the tenant is allowed). Add a global banner in Layout.jsx explaining view_only/suspended and disable write actions, or at minimum show the banner. Make sure the trial-ending state shows the days left.

gaps.what: No test or guard pins the 30-day trial and the trial-status creation shape in createWineBar. The other guarantees are covered by guard_logic_test.
gaps.fix: Extract computeTrialEnd into an import-free module, or add a deno test asserting that the trial_end_at delta is exactly 30 days and billing_status is 'trial'. Optionally add a CI check that grep finds no function writing billing_status other than createWineBar.

title: Multi-tenant data isolation (RLS)
evidence:
Repo: `npm run validate:rls` passes (19 entities, 13 tenant-scoped), and `npm run validate:tenant-roles` passes. CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs both as blocking steps, plus check:guards and deno test. scripts/lib/entity-rls-rules.mjs is adapted from StockFlow's checker for tenant_id. It enforces the `data.` entity prefix, the `{{user.data.*}}` user templates, the tenant equality on read, and the `role:admin` service branch on read/create/update/delete.

Deployed schema: I read all 19 entities with list_entity_schemas (appId 6ab41c2a89f592a0eca074d2) and compared them with base44/entities/*.jsonc. RLS blocks match the repo for every entity checked.
- The 13 tenant-scoped entities read with `$or[data.tenant_id == {{user.data.tenant_id}}, role:admin]`. Create/update/delete are `role:admin` only, which suits Sommel because every write goes through Safe functions as the service role.
- Product, Attendance and StaffPin have read limited to `role:admin`. This is deliberate: the Product.jsonc header documents that costs are redacted by the `catalog` function, and Attendance/StaffPin are served through functions.
- SupportTicket create also allows the tenant branch.
- WineBar update is `$or[role:admin, $and[id == tenant_id, user_condition{data.app_role:bar_admin}]]`. That is a tenant-scoped role inside `$and`, which Module 24 allows. There are no `user_condition` entries with sibling keys, so the liuma defect does not apply.
- WineBar billing_status, trial_end_at, current_period_end, plan and owner_id carry `rls.write: role:admin` in the deployed schema (Module 19).
- User.tenant_id and User.app_role carry `rls.write: false`.
- OrderItem.unit_cost, InventoryItem.unit_cost and InventoryMovement.unit_cost have `rls.read` limited to the platform tier.

Live data: only h.josepablo@gmail.com holds built-in role admin. All other users are role `user`, with tenant_id and app_role on the data fields.

Compared with the StockFlow reference: same four-op shape and same checker. Sommel's tenant-roles checker is byte-identical to shared/tenant-roles/check-tenant-roles.mjs.

Not verified: no authenticated session as a restricted user of a second tenant, so I checked the rules by reading them, not by exercising them. I made no writes.

gaps.what: Nothing in AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md or docs/ records a dated Module 14 isolation audit that names the deployed-vs-repo diff and what could not be verified. docs/plan-tecnico.md only schedules the audit for week 7. Module 4's deployed-schema check is therefore done but undocumented. There are already 2 real tenants and 7 users in live data.
gaps.fix: Add a dated 'Módulo 4/14' section to AGENTS.md or docs recording the result above. It should say the deployed schema matches the repo for all 19 entities, list the deliberate admin-only reads (Product, Attendance, StaffPin) and the field locks, and state that a restricted second-tenant session was not verified.

gaps.what: Minor and optional, not a standard requirement: SupportTicket create allows the tenant branch, so a tenant member can raw-create a ticket with arbitrary status or fields. The tenant_id is pinned by the rule, so this is not a cross-tenant issue.
gaps.fix: Route ticket creation only through a Safe function and make create `role:admin` only, or leave it as is. This is optional.
gaps.blocked_on: user decision

title: Granular permissions
evidence: DONE: (a) Client registry src/lib/permissionRegistry.js has 23 'Section:action' keys with bar_admin/staff defaults. PermissionContext.jsx and usePermission.js are split and use the same resolvePermission precedence (platform/bar_admin, then override, then default, then deny). Layout.jsx and App.jsx RequirePermission gate nav and routes. (b) Server side: base44/functions/*/_guard.ts calls requireContext, which re-reads User with asServiceRole (module 22). hasPermission reads PermissionProfile by tenant+role. My scan of every base44/functions/*/handlers/*.ts file found requirePermission on all of them. requireWritable (billing_status view_only/suspended gives 402) is present on all write handlers. The exceptions are read-only handlers, attendance resetPin/setMyPin/roster/records, manageStaff (inline billing gate on invite/setRole/removeMember, bar_admin-only) and the retired processSale (410). (c) Zero direct client writes except SuperAdmin.jsx:36 WineBar.update billing_status. That one is platform-admin-only, the field is RLS-locked to role:admin, and it is documented as a TODO exception. (d) Drift check: scripts/generate-guards.mjs generates the AUTOGEN block, npm run check:guards runs in .github/workflows/ci.yml, and deno test base44/tests/ runs guard_logic_test.ts. It covers the resolvePermission precedence, unknown-key deny and no-role deny. (e) PermissionProfile deployed schema (live list_entity_schemas) matches the repo: read is tenant-scoped, create/update/delete are role:admin only, so staff cannot rewrite their own profile. MISSING: the write side of overrides and the admin Permisos screen. Live query of PermissionProfile returned 0 rows. The deployed base44/functions has no 'permissions' function (13 groups: reports, orders, printing, processSale, payments, catalog, inventory, shifts, manageStaff, settings, createWineBar, stations, attendance). docs/plan-tecnico.md:86 plans 'permissions: getProfile, upsertProfile' and PermissionProfile.jsonc:7 references upsertProfile, but grep of src/, base44/ and scripts/ finds no implementation. src/pages has no Permisos/PermissionAdmin page and App.jsx has no such route. Overrides (step 2 of the precedence) are therefore unreachable in practice: a bar_admin cannot see or change what staff can do. STANDARD.md section 3 calls this screen a requirement and the CHECKLIST Module 3 item repeats it. Not verified: authenticated session as staff (no credentials). Minor: order is loadOwned, then permission, then requireWritable. The standard text says billing is checked before permission; the StockFlow reference does permission first, so I am not flagging it.

gaps.what: No server writer for PermissionProfile: the planned 'permissions' function (getProfile/upsertProfile) was never built. Entity RLS allows only role:admin to write, so no bar_admin can persist an override. Live table has 0 rows.
gaps.fix: Add a permissions group (entry.ts + _guard.ts and _guard_logic.ts copies via generate-guards, handlers getProfile and upsertProfile). upsertProfile: requireContext, then require ctx.isPlatform or appRole==='bar_admin', then requireWritable. Validate role in {bar_admin,staff} (or restrict edits to staff), keep only keys that exist in PERMISSION_DEFAULTS with boolean values, reject unknown keys, re-derive tenant_id from ctx (never from the body), find or create the row by tenant_id+role via asServiceRole, and write. Add logic tests in base44/tests/. Register the new group in the generate-guards targets and check the maxFunctions budget (currently 40). Deploy with npm run deploy and verify by calling an action only the new code has.
gaps.blocked_on: Deploy and Publish need an authenticated Base44 CLI/panel (operator); the code itself can be written by an agent alone.

gaps.what: No admin-facing 'Permisos' screen. The standard requires a matrix page rendering the same registry.
gaps.fix: Create src/pages/Permisos.jsx gated to bar_admin/platform. Render PERMISSION_DEFAULTS grouped by section (prefix before ':') with one column per action, a tri-state group checkbox per section, per-key overrides for the staff role, and an explicit edit/read-only toggle. Persist each change immediately through permissions.upsertProfile. Show defaults vs overrides, and add a Layout nav entry (bar_admin only) and a route in App.jsx. Refresh PermissionContext after saving. Also add an action label/description map in the registry so the matrix has readable names.
gaps.blocked_on: Depends on the permissions function gap above (can be built in the same PR). Deploying the site needs the operator.

gaps.what: The 'Permisos' matrix cannot cover 'everything the app manages' because staff-management actions (manageStaff invite/setRole/removeMember/revokeInvite, PIN reset) are gated by a hardcoded bar_admin check, not registry keys. Also manageStaff/revokeInvite has no billing gate. The standard says member management is gated by Module 3 (CHECKLIST Module 7 line).
gaps.fix: Add registry keys (e.g. 'Equipo:invitar', 'Equipo:cambiar_rol', 'Equipo:quitar') with bar_admin:true, staff:false. Make manageStaff resolve them with resolvePermission and PermissionProfile. Note manageStaff is intentionally standalone and does not use _guard.ts, so it needs a resolver import or an inline copy of the AUTOGEN block. Add requireWritable to revokeInvite. Keep the last-admin and owner protections as they are. This is optional depth beyond the strict module 3 text; prioritise the two gaps above first.
gaps.blocked_on: Product decision: should staff ever be allowed to manage the team? Default keys stay false so behaviour is unchanged.

gaps.what: SuperAdmin.jsx writes WineBar.billing_status directly from the client (own TODO admits it violates the 'no direct client writes' rule). It is not exploitable, because it is role:admin-only and the field is RLS-locked. It also overlaps module 1, where MC should own billing_status.
gaps.fix: Route it through a platform-only Safe function action, or remove the manual control if Mission Control now owns billing_status. Update the TODO comment accordingly.
gaps.blocked_on: Product/operator decision on whether Mission Control owns billing_status for Sommel (module 1).

gaps.what: The drift check and the resolver tests exist, but the CHECKLIST gate also expects the server to be tested against overrides via the real hasPermission path. That is partially covered: resolvePermission is tested, but the PermissionProfile lookup (tenant+role filter) is not. Nothing exercises an override end to end because no profile can be written.
gaps.fix: After the writer exists, add a test that pins the profile lookup key (tenant_id+role) and the override shape produced by upsertProfile against what hasPermission reads, e.g. a shared pure normalizer in _guard_logic.ts.

title: Health & latency reporting
evidence:
The repo has no health or ping endpoint.
- /home/user/sommel/base44/functions/ holds 13 groups: attendance, catalog, createWineBar, inventory, manageStaff, orders, payments, printing, processSale, reports, settings, shifts and stations. There is no acaciaControl directory.
- grep for ping, health and acaciaControl across base44/, src/, scripts/ and docs/ finds only planning text. docs/plan-tecnico.md:87 lists "`acaciaControl` | ping (salud, módulo 5), license, tickets, usage" as a future endpoint. base44/entities/AppSession.jsonc:4 mentions the bridge in a comment.
- The Base44 deployed tree (read-only list_directory on appId 6ab41c2a89f592a0eca074d2, base44/functions) shows the same 13 directories and no acaciaControl.
- Mission Control cannot probe Sommel. /home/user/acacia-mission-control/api/_lib/sync/syncHealth.js probes every backend='base44' app with callBridge(app,'ping') and accepts out.ok, out.pong or out.data.ok. It measures latency itself and marks the app degraded above 2000ms. A repo-wide grep of Mission Control finds no "sommel" in any source, migration or seed, so no apps row exists and no app_health row can be written.
- The verification gate is "an app_health row with status: ok dated today". That is impossible today.
- Reference: /home/user/stockflow/base44/functions/acaciaControl/entry.ts:44-45 answers ping with `{ ok: true, pong: true }`. The standard asks for a real backend round-trip, and Mission Control only times the call from outside, so Sommel's ping should read one row from an entity.
- The endpoint budget is not a blocker. base44.app.json sets maxFunctions to 40 and Sommel has 13 groups. plan-tecnico.md counts about 14 endpoints, and acaciaControl is one of them.
- Not checked: the live site (curl to sommel.acaciaco.com.mx), because module 5 does not depend on it.

gaps.what: There is no acaciaControl function, so no health endpoint exists in the repo or in the deployed backend.
gaps.fix: Create base44/functions/acaciaControl/entry.ts with HMAC verification and an `action` switch. `ping` must do a real store round-trip using asServiceRole, for example `sr.entities.WineBar.list('-created_date', 1)` or `Tenant.list`, inside try/catch. It returns `{ok:true,pong:true}` on success and a 5xx or `{ok:false,error}` if the read fails. Copy the shared verifier byte for byte from acaciaSign.ts in shared/bridge/ (module 15, verifyFrom with ACACIA_APP_SLUG=sommel and ACCEPT_LEGACY_MASTER=false) and from stockflow's acaciaControl/_acaciaSign.ts. `ping` shares its shell with license, tickets and usage (modules 8 and 15), so build the shell once. A ping-only first cut is acceptable. Add a unit test that a bad signature is rejected. Comply with the `validate:functions` budget (maxFunctions 40).

gaps.what: The function is not deployed, so nothing answers Mission Control's probe.
gaps.fix: Run `npm run deploy` from the sommel directory, then click Publish in the Base44 panel. The CLI's `unchanged` is not proof (2026-09-24 note). Verify by content: call ping with a valid signature and read the pong. Calling an action only the new code has and getting `unknown action` means the old code is still live.
gaps.blocked_on: Base44 CLI or panel access and an authenticated operator. The MCP here is read-only for this task.

gaps.what: Sommel is not registered in Mission Control, so no health row is ever written.
gaps.fix: Add an `apps` row (id sommel, backend base44, external_id 6ab41c2a89f592a0eca074d2, url https://sommel.acaciaco.com.mx) via a new migration and seed in /home/user/acacia-mission-control/supabase/migrations. Put the per-app token in BASE44_TOKEN_6AB41C2A89F592A0ECA074D2 or use the shared BASE44_SERVICE_TOKEN. Set ACACIA_APP_SLUG=sommel and INGEST_HMAC_SECRET (the shared master) in Sommel's secrets. Then run 'Sincronizar ahora' and confirm an app_health row with status ok and latency_ms today, and a sync with no `rejected the derived key` warnings. This overlaps modules 15, 16 and 17.
gaps.blocked_on: Mission Control repo write access, Supabase migration apply, and Vercel or Base44 secret access. The operator (Alby) must set the secrets.

gaps.what: Do not build a second in-app status page. The standard allows only a thin one fed from the same signal. Nothing exists today, so nothing needs to be done.
gaps.fix: None. If an in-app status is added later, read it from acaciaControl.ping or app_health, not from a separate signal.

title: Account & danger zone
evidence: Done: (a) Profile/org edit: src/pages/Ajustes.jsx + components/settings (TicketForm name/address/RFC/ticket header-footer, PaymentMethodsCard, CorteEmailsCard) via base44/functions/settings (get/update), gated by 'Ajustes:editar' (permissionRegistry.js:40) with requirePermission + requireWritable (billing gate). (b) Member mgmt: src/pages/Staff.jsx + base44/functions/manageStaff/entry.ts (list, invite, revokeInvite, setRole, removeMember) with server re-derived tenant, target read from tenant's own User.filter, guards checkSetRole/checkRemoveMember (owner_locked, last_admin, self_remove), billing gate 402, access-cut verified by re-read, StaffPin/Attendance cleanup. Partial-credit gap: gate is a bespoke `appRole !== 'bar_admin' && !isPlatformAdmin` check (entry.ts ~line 58), not hasPermission()/Module 3; registry has no Staff key. Note: setRole to bar_admin IS the "promote member to tenant admin" (multiple bar_admins supported, last_admin protected, owner locked). Missing: no danger zone anywhere in src (grep for export/delete/eliminar/peligro finds nothing outside UI primitives and attendance strings). No `account` function exists in base44/functions (list: attendance catalog createWineBar inventory manageStaff orders payments printing processSale reports settings shifts stations) although docs/plan-tecnico.md:85 plans `account | exportData, deleteMyAccount, deleteBar | 7`. No delete-my-account, no delete-tenant, no export, no delegate/transfer owner (WineBar.owner_id is RLS-locked and manageStaff returns 'owner_locked', so there is no path to hand the bar over except via ACACIA). No read-only billing_status/plan display in Ajustes or Layout (billing_status appears in src only in SuperAdmin.jsx, platform view). Positive: billing_status/trial_end_at/current_period_end/plan/owner_id carry rls.write admin in WineBar.jsonc. Did not run live schema/curl checks; conclusions are from repo code.

gaps.what: No data export (self-service) anywhere
gaps.fix: Add `account` function group (router + handlers) with exportData: re-derive tenant from stored User via asServiceRole, requirePermission('Ajustes:exportar'), NO billing gate (read-only, suspended tenants must be able to export), return WineBar row plus all tenant-scoped entities (BarTable, CashMovement, Category, InventoryItem, InventoryMovement, Order, OrderItem, Payment, PermissionProfile, PrintJob, Product, Shift, StaffInvite, StaffPin, Attendance, SupportTicket, AppSession) filtered by verified tenant_id; per-entity failure returns empty + errors[] and UI warns; exclude other users' PII beyond roster. title: Multi-tenant isolation audit
evidence:
The isolation itself checks out, but the audit has never been recorded, and the standard says "audited" means a dated line in the app's CLAUDE.md.

Recording gap:
- /home/user/sommel/CLAUDE.md only says "See AGENTS.md". AGENTS.md is generic Base44 boilerplate with no audit section.

The only references are docs/plan-tecnico.md, which schedules it for "Fase 4" (line 146) and says each entity or function change must repeat the audit and be noted in CLAUDE.md (line 170). That never happened, although entities and functions changed several times (Entrega 2, Checador, Staff invites).

What I read against the deployed app 6ab41c2a89f592a0eca074d2:

1. Entities.
- `list_entity_schemas` returns 19 entities. Their RLS matches the repo's base44/entities/*.jsonc in every rule I compared.
- Local checks pass: `validate:rls` (19 entities, 13 tenant-scoped), `validate:tenant-roles` and `check:guards`. I ran them.
- Tenant-scoped reads use `$or[{data.tenant_id:{{user.data.tenant_id}}},{user_condition:{role:admin}}]`. Both halves are correct, and there is no sibling-key `user_condition` (the liuma defect).
- Every entity's create/update/delete is admin-only (service role). The only exceptions are AppSession, which is keyed to `created_by_id`, and SupportTicket, whose create is tenant-scoped and whose update/delete are admin-only.
- Product, Attendance and StaffPin are read admin-only. That is deliberate, so cost and PINs never reach a tenant's browser.
- Field locks are in place. `unit_cost` has admin-only read on OrderItem, InventoryItem and InventoryMovement.

2. Backend functions (13 endpoints).
- `requireContext` re-reads `User` with asServiceRole and derives tenantId, appRole and isPlatform from that row.
- `loadOwned` compares against the stored row's `tenant_id`, and a missing row and a cross-tenant row both answer 404 (no existence oracle).
- Every handler except `importMenu` calls `requirePermission` or `hasPermission`. `importMenu` is platform-only and takes `tenant_id` from the body, which is acceptable because it checks `ctx.isPlatform` and that the WineBar exists.
- `addItems`, `upsertProduct` and the inventory handlers take `tenant_id` from the stored row, not from `ctx`.
- `processSale` is retired (returns 410).
- `manageStaff` re-derives tenant and role. Cross-bar targets are unreachable because the member list is filtered by tenant, and `revokeInvite` compares the stored `tenant_id`.
- `claimInvite` looks up by the caller's stored email.
- `createWineBar` answers 409 to anyone who already has a tenant.

3. Field locks on tenant-written data.
- WineBar `billing_status`, `trial_end_at`, `current_period_end`, `plan` and `owner_id` are admin-write-only, matching the repo.
- `User.tenant_id` and `User.app_role` are `write:false`.
- Live `User` rows: 7. The only role admin is h.josepablo@gmail.com. The rest are role `user`, across two real tenants (6abaa0c3… and 6abaacb1…) plus one tenantless user.

4. Reports and exports.
- `reports.summary` scopes everything by `ctx.tenantId` and gates cost and corte visibility with `hasPermission`.
- Client reads all filter by `tenant_id`, and RLS backs them up.

5. Outbound.
- Corte email recipients come from the stored `WineBar.corte_emails` (`shifts/_shared.ts:142`). `resendEmail` uses `loadOwned` on the shift.
- Invite email goes to the address the bar_admin typed, which is the intended behaviour.

6. Tenant pointer.
- Only `createWineBar`, `claimInvite` and `manageStaff` write it, all as service role. `Onboarding.jsx` runs only for tenantless users, so there is no prior-tenant cache to leak.

7. Deployed schema versus repo: matches on RLS and field locks (compared above).

title: A shipped security fix needs a guard of its own
evidence:
Live read of the deployed schema (list_entity_schemas, appId 6ab41c2a89f592a0eca074d2, 19 entities read across 3 calls) against base44/entities/*.jsonc. In every entity that was read, the locks match the repo:
- User.tenant_id and User.app_role have rls.write:false.
- WineBar.billing_status, trial_end_at, current_period_end, plan and owner_id have rls.write:{role:admin}.
- The unit_cost fields on OrderItem, InventoryItem and InventoryMovement have rls.read admin-only.
- Product.read and Attendance.read are admin-only at the entity level.
- StaffInvite, PermissionProfile and StaffPin are admin-write only.
So there is no drift on the locks I compared. I did not diff every description byte for byte.

What exists:
- The WineBar licence fields carry "Módulo 19" descriptions that say what breaks if the lock is removed (e.g. "cualquier miembro del bar podría reactivar su propio bar suspendido").
- The User locks state the mechanism and the writer ("Server-authoritative... write:false para que nadie se dé bar_admin con updateMe").
- CI runs validate:rls, validate:tenant-roles (Module 24; covers only the User tenant pointer and role locks) and check:guards.

Gaps:
- Rationale for the OrderItem.unit_cost lock is not in the deployed descriptions. The read-lock descriptions on InventoryItem and InventoryMovement unit_cost, and WineBar.owner_id, are one-liners with no what-breaks-if-removed. Point 1 asks for the operation governed and what breaks; only User (write:false) and the WineBar licence fields state the operation explicitly. OrderItem.unit_cost says "se bloquea a la plataforma" without saying read, and the InventoryItem/InventoryMovement/owner_id descriptions do not name the operation at all.
- The entity-level read locks on Product and Attendance (and the admin-only write on Order, Payment, Shift, CashMovement, StaffInvite, PermissionProfile and StaffPin) are explained only in .jsonc // comments. Comments are not deployed, and the live Product and Attendance schemas carry no explanation, so an in-app Base44 builder inspecting only the live schema sees no reason for them. A builder debugging "products don't load" could loosen Product.read.
- Nothing in the repo asserts that the locks survive. No test or script fails if billing_status, plan or unit_cost loses its rls block, if a Módulo-19 description is deleted, or if Product.read is loosened. validate-entity-rls.mjs checks path syntax and that the admin branch is present, not the presence of specific locks.
- Point 4 (repo file agrees with deployed schema) has no tool. No script or workflow diffs the deployed schema against the repo files; I did it by hand here.
- Point 5 has no artefact. No dated lock inventory or drift-audit record exists in docs/ or AGENTS.md, and plan-tecnico.md §4 only schedules the Module 14 audit.
- AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are stubs with no Module 19 rules (state the mechanism first, put the lock back if the symptom persists, check both surfaces).
- The Verification gates row for 19 reads "deployed schema still shows it, repo agrees, description states rationale". The first two hold today; the third is only partly true (see above).

gaps.what: Lock descriptions do not all state the governed operation and what breaks if removed. The rationale for the OrderItem.unit_cost lock is not in the deployed descriptions.
gaps.fix: Rewrite the descriptions of WineBar.owner_id, OrderItem.unit_cost, InventoryItem.unit_cost and InventoryMovement.unit_cost. Each should say: which operation the lock governs (read vs write, and that it does not affect the other), who legitimately writes or reads the field, and what security hole opens if the lock is removed. Add an equivalent line to User.role. Keep the wording in the repo .jsonc identical to the deployed schema.
gaps.blocked_on: Repo edit is solo-doable. Reaching the live schema needs an operator to run npm run deploy:entities, or update_entity_schema via the Base44 MCP.

gaps.what: Entity-level locks (Product.read admin-only, Attendance.read admin-only, admin-only writes on the server-written entities) are documented only in // comments that never reach the deployed schema.
gaps.fix: Move the rationale into schema text that is deployed. First check whether Base44 accepts a top-level entity description. If it does, use it. If not, put it in the description of a stable field, e.g. Product.cost and tenant_id, Attendance.clock_in, Order.total. State the operation (read) and why (variants[].cost cannot be field-locked, so nobody may read Product directly and catalog.listProducts redacts). Also state that writes go only through Safe functions, and that loosening the lock will not fix a display or read-resolution symptom.
gaps.blocked_on: Deploy to the live schema needs an operator (deploy:entities or the MCP).

gaps.what: No automated guard that the security locks stay in the repo files. Removing a lock or its rationale would pass CI.
gaps.fix: Add scripts/validate-locks.mjs (npm run validate:locks, wired into ci.yml) plus a Deno test. It holds an explicit manifest, one entry per lock: User.tenant_id and app_role rls.write:false; WineBar.billing_status, trial_end_at, current_period_end, plan and owner_id rls.write admin; OrderItem, InventoryItem and InventoryMovement unit_cost rls.read admin; Product.read and Attendance.read admin; and the admin-only create/update/delete on the server-written entities. It fails if a lock is missing or changed, or if the field description is shorter than a minimum or lacks a required keyword (e.g. 'Módulo 19' plus the operation word). A new lock must be added to the manifest deliberately. Cover Module 1's billing_status, the Module 14 field locks and the tenant pointer, as point 5 lists.

gaps.what: No repo-vs-deployed drift check (point 4) and no dated lock audit (point 5).
gaps.fix: Add scripts/check-lock-drift.mjs that takes the JSON output of list_entity_schemas (or reads it via the Base44 API when a token is present). It compares the manifest entries against it for both the rule and the description, and exits 1 on any difference. Document the run command. Add a dated 'Locks audited' section to docs listing each lock, deployed vs repo verdict, and what could not be verified. Repeat it whenever an entity, function or role is added, alongside the Module 14 re-audit. As of 2026-09-29 the by-hand comparison found no drift in the entities read, and that result can seed the first entry.
gaps.blocked_on: Running it against the live app needs the Base44 CLI/API token or an MCP session; the script and doc are solo-doable.

gaps.what: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md contain no Module 19 rules or lock inventory, so a debugging session (git agent, Base44 in-app builder, teammate) has no warning.
gaps.fix: Add a section to AGENTS.md, not the CLAUDE.md pointer. List the locks with the operation each governs. Add the rules: an rls.write rule never affects reads and a read rule never affects writes; state and prove the mechanism before loosening; if the symptom persists, put the lock back first; after any live schema edit, update the .jsonc in the same session and run validate:locks. Also copy the essentials into base44 app-level instructions so the in-app builder sees them.

title: Client navigation chrome survives a reload
evidence:
Read STANDARD.md section 23 and the module 23 row of Verification gates, then src/components/Layout.jsx and src/App.jsx in /home/user/sommel. I did not run live checks or a browser reload.

Point 1 is met. Layout.jsx line ~86 computes `active` on every render from `useLocation().pathname` (`pathname === it.to || pathname.startsWith(it.to)`). There is no mount-time `useState` and no one-shot animation for the highlight. Layout sits inside the ProtectedRoute and RequireTenant routes, so the active item follows the route once auth resolves. App.jsx shows a full-screen spinner while `isLoadingAuth` is true, so no wrong highlight is drawn in the meantime.

Point 3 is met. `grep "location.reload\|reload()" src` finds no `window.location.reload` at all. The only `reload()` calls are data reloads in Orden.jsx and useOrderRealtime.js, not page reloads. Nothing in the app resets navigation on purpose.

Point 2 is only partly met. The nav has no collapsible groups: it is a flat list of up to 13 items with no manual expand or collapse state. But `<nav className="flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-y-auto">` is a scrollable menu. The standard names "a scroll position inside a long menu" as chrome state that must persist via `sessionStorage`, keyed by a stable string and restored synchronously on mount. Sommel has no `sessionStorage` use anywhere in src. On a short viewport a reload therefore snaps the sidebar back to the top, and a lower item such as Ajustes or Staff can end up scrolled out of view after F5.

Side observations, not standard requirements. The permission-gated items (`can()`) are computed while the PermissionProfile is still loading, so the list can change once the overrides arrive. That shifts the layout but does not affect the highlight. `src/components/ui/sidebar.jsx` is the unused shadcn component; its `sidebar_state` cookie is not wired to anything.

The checks in the "nav survives reload" row (hard-reload a deep route, expand a group, reload again) can only be done in a browser.

gaps.what: The sidebar's scroll position (nav with overflow-y-auto) is not persisted across reload. The standard (section 23, point 2) requires non-route-derived nav state, explicitly including scroll position inside a long menu, to be stored in sessionStorage and restored synchronously on mount.
gaps.fix: In Layout.jsx, add a ref on the <nav>. Restore its scrollTop synchronously with useLayoutEffect on mount from a stable sessionStorage key (e.g. 'acacia.nav.scroll.sommel'), inside try/catch. Save the value on scroll (throttled or on pagehide/beforeunload). Do not use localStorage or a backend field. Optionally call scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'}) on the active item when it is outside the visible area. Keep the item-list filtering unchanged. Consider a small unit test with jsdom or a Playwright step that scrolls the nav, reloads, and asserts the same scrollTop.

gaps.what: No automated guard for the module 23 claim. The gates table says to hard-reload a deep route and check the highlight, then reload again with state expanded. Sommel's smoke suite does not cover this (I did not confirm whether a tests/smoke directory exists; the repo listing showed none).
gaps.fix: Optional: once the scroll persistence above exists, add a Playwright assertion in the app's smoke config or a local test that reloads /reportes or /ajustes while authenticated and checks the highlighted item and nav scrollTop. This needs an authenticated session, so it may only be feasible as a manual check documented in the docs.
gaps.blocked_on: Authenticated test session or a decision to document this as a manual verification step only
